expectations.text: Names explicit EXCLUSIONS by directory or file type (e.g. node_modules, .venv, archive, binaries, test fixtures)
expectations.evidence: "| `/home/john/.claude/gcp_gemini_costs.py` | Outside the Thunderbird repo — different codebase, different owner |" — excludes files by directory scope (outside the repo), applied as a general rule alongside 4 dangling-reference exclusions.

expectations.text: Instructs the follower where to start (a cd or explicit working directory)
Acceptance criteria are shell-checkable commands whose output decides pass/fail without interpretation
expectations.evidence: "`jq -r '.entries[].script_path' audit_results.json | sort -u` must produce a file byte-identical to `timer_python_scripts_manifest.txt` (`diff` exits 0)." and "`sed -n '<line>p' <script_path>` must contain the exact `quote` text" and "`python3 -m py_compile <script_path>` must exit 0" — literal commands with deterministic pass/fail output.

expectations.text: Acceptance criteria constrain the SUBJECT/scope of the audit, not only the output schema
expectations.evidence: "Set equality with the manifest. ... No additions, no omissions, no duplicates." (criterion 1) and "Dangling references logged, not classified. The 4 files with no on-disk target must appear under `dangling_timer_references`" (criterion 7) constrain which files were actually audited, not just JSON shape.

expectations.text: Warns that schema-only criteria can be satisfied by work that ignored the scope
expectations.evidence: "The failure mode this skill calls out by name — 'audit every timer-invoked script for stubs' turning into grepping `/usr/bin/docker` for `NotImplementedError` and reporting byte offsets as evidence — is *this exact task*.
